about: Scenes of the scene stand (README.md). Positions in blocks: +X east, +Z south; ground = top of the grass of the flat world. Launch bearings: degrees from south toward east. Every strike is its own command with spread 0 at a fixed aim point (a Vogel sunflower over the spread disc, turned per salvo and wave: the same for every version, unlike the salvo spread of Incoming, which takes the shared world random), from launch point i mod launchers, gap_s apart from one point, straight via the aim point; server_config is the world rule written to config/incoming-server.toml (drone_flight_time at its minimum: the flight is never shorter than the direct path). An impact is a projectile leaving the world near the target and its own explosion with a warhead damage type (warheads): a crash before arming is a vanilla explosion and does not count. Launch close-ups (launch): the camera stands 30 m beside the launch point at eye height and looks at it; the target is far downrange to the side, so impacts stay out of the frame; windows are timed from the command, the scene does not wait for impacts (they come last in the plan). Nuclear scenes (bursts): ground bursts by `incoming nuke now at` (a host command: no flight), the camera 2.8 km from the first burst 35 m above the ground facing its cloud, inside the dust wall from about +100 s; windows are timed from the first burst (nuke_view: `show` 2–60 s holds the flash and the wave's passage, `entry` 60.5–119.5 s the dust wall reaching the camera and, in nuke2, the second burst from its detonation (60.5 s, the window opens on it), `dust` +2…+6 min the dust around the camera; only the frame at each window end and half a second after it go unmeasured), after every other scene: a burst ruins and loads the world for minutes.
